description: The dependency dashboard is on: it is the only place that shows what Renovate tried and could not land, which the weekly pull request never mentions.
The commit pins.yml adds to finish a raise is not taken as someone else's edit, so Renovate still rebases and updates its branch.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Off, so that a vulnerability fix rides in the one weekly pull request like every other raise instead of arriving on its own branch outside the schedule.

lockFileMaintenance.description: The lock files regenerated the day after the raises, which is where the transitive crates and packages move.

packageRules.description: One pull request for everything, majors included. Every check has to pass before anything merges, so separate pull requests would only be that many rounds of CI for one week's raises.
steamcmd's version is a Unix timestamp, so every raise is a jump of thousands; best-practices refuses any major jump above 500 as a guard against date-like versions, which this is on purpose.
The toolchain is raised by the Rust manager below, together with the crate's rust-version from the same release list; Renovate's own rust-toolchain manager would raise the same line a second time.
Cargo.toml names the version tested, not a floor, so a raise moves it along with the lock file.
The Homebrew formula and the Scoop manifest are written by each release from its own signed checksums; Renovate's homebrew manager would raise one of the formula's archives and leave the others.
An image's tag is a bare number, which its digest can hold too. Renovate changes the first copy alone, the tag, and the digest keeps its own replacement.

steamcmd.description: Valve's manifest is KeyValues, not JSON, so it is read as plain text, one release per line, and the transform keeps the one line that holds the version.

fedora.description: Fedora's image tags from Docker Hub's tag list, not the registry: rawhide carries the next release's number there, and the list shows which number `latest` is. That number and those below it are the releases, each with its digest.
transformTemplates: ($latest := results[name = 'latest'].digest; $top := $number(results[digest = $latest and $match(name, /^[0-9]+$/)].name); {"releases": results[$type(digest) = 'string' and $match(name, /^[0-9]+$/) and $number(name) <= $top].{"version": name, "digest": digest}})

customManagers.description: Rust: the toolchain CI and developers build with, the rust-version the crate declares, which is the same version on purpose, and the README's badge naming it.

Valve's steamcmd manifests, one per system, pinned byte for byte in pins/. Only the version inside a pin can be raised here; .github/workflows/pins.yml then commits Valve's manifest for that version to the branch, so the pull request carries the whole pin.

A NuGet package pinned in a .github script: ConPTY in conpty.sh, BinSkim in binskim.sh. Only the version can be raised here, and nuget.org gives no digest, so .github/workflows/pins.yml writes the SHA-256 on the branch. A version is three or four numbers, which leaves preview versions out.
A container image by tag and digest in an action of this repository: the bare Debian and Fedora the Linux packages are installed on. The tag and the digest move together.

A release tag with the SHA-256 of the asset downloaded on the next line, in a workflow or an action of this repository: actionlint, cargo-deny, nFPM and the like. The tag and the digest move together.
A tag with the commit it names on the next line: Scoop's own code, which the packages workflow fetches by commit. The tag and the commit move together.
A tool fetched by version in a workflow, under the comment naming where its versions come from: cargo-fuzz and cargo-auditable as `..._VERSION:`, syft as an action's `...-version:` input.
The runner images inside a job matrix, or handed to one through a variable, which the github-actions manager does not read.
